user_requirements: CONSOLIDATED FINAL PACKAGE REVIEW of the Nikki Christian exit (legal drafts — not an acquisition analysis). Corpus: SPA_DRAFT_V7.md (the Share Sale Agreement, v7), ADVISORY_AGREEMENT.md (the separate advisory & consulting agreement), deal_facts.txt (READ FIRST — includes the CLIENT-PROTECTION REQUIREMENTS and the RESTRAINT RESCOPE sections describing the newest changes), and research_comparable_exits.txt (research memo on comparable exits, restraint case law, earn-out pitfalls, PSPLA regulatory requirements, s149 practice). Deliver five passes: (1) RESTRAINT RESCOPE VERIFICATION — does v7 implement the purchaser's rescoped intent exactly: security consulting/advisory OUTSIDE guarding is permitted; operational guarding businesses restrained; the current portfolio (24-month lookback clients) fully off-limits including for consulting/advisory/training/review; company IP developed during the Vendor's tenure gated behind prior written confirmation (cl 12A)? Stress-test the new boundary: can the consulting permission in 10.4(c) be stretched to cover disguised operational work (e.g. 'consulting' that embeds guard supply via subcontractors)? Is the 12A IP gate enforceable and is the 12A.3 memory carve-out correctly scoped (not swallowing the gate)? (2) CLIENT-PROTECTION LAYER REVIEW (this replaces the interrupted round 4) — cl 4.5 (ASG-only liaison role, both-companies good-faith duty), cl 11.4 (Client Protection Period = settlement to 1 Oct 2026), cl 11.5 (no client contact without written confirmation; advisory-services exception), cl 11.6 (client-departure set-off trigger with 'directly contributed to in any capacity' causation): requirement fidelity, penalty-doctrine risk (is 11.6 defensible or does it make the Vendor an insurer of retention?), burden-of-proof workability, interactions with 15.1's material-breach machinery. (3) CROSS-DOCUMENT CONSISTENCY — every reference between the two documents must resolve: the Advisory Agreement's Background B cites SPA clause 10.4(c) which v7 RENUMBERED to 10.4(d) — verify and flag every cross-reference both ways (advisory cl 1.2 vs SPA 11.5; advisory cl 6.1 vs SPA 12/14.4; advisory cl 10.1 vs SPA 17; commission scheme vs SPA restraints — a new client Nikki introduces is not a 'client' under SPA 11.2's lookback definition, verify no conflict); also verify the advisory agreement's terms match deal_facts (13% commission mechanics, $1,500/month, 6 hours over 2 days minimum, $100+GST extras, withhold/still-paid rules, quarterly renewal + 90-day notice — note the internal tension between a 3-month term and a 90-day notice period and recommend how the solicitors should resolve it). (4) COMPLIANCE SWEEP — against the research memo: PSPLA officer-change prior-approval/notification requirements (SPA 14.3 adequacy; whether the advisory QC/client-facing role may require the Vendor to hold a current Certificate of Approval — flag prominently); s149 employment settlement handling; contractor-vs-employee risk in the advisory agreement (6 fixed hours, monthly retainer, direction by a named individual — does it look like employment? recommend protective language if needed); regulatory-integrity constraint (open PSPLA/CIPU process) across BOTH documents. (5) RECOMMENDATIONS — informed by the research memo's comparable-exit findings, list concrete recommendations for the package: dispute-cheap commission calculation (expert-determination option), margin/standard-rates protection on the 13% commission, information/audit rights for the Advisor on commission calculation, anything the comparable-exit history (Gwin advisory, Pro Host client-consent) suggests. Output: findings with severity (BLOCKER/RECOMMENDED/OPTIONAL) and exact fix wording per document, a cross-reference resolution table, the compliance verdict, the recommendations list, and a final transmission verdict for the package.
